questions.stem: The shoulder joint complex consists of:
options: Two true joints and three sliding spaces
Three true joints: scapulohumeral, sternocostoclavicular, acromioclavicular
Two sliding spaces: the subacromiodeltoid serous bursa and the scapulothoracic joint
Five true joints
Only the scapulohumeral joint
questions.explanation: 5 synergistic joints: 3 true joints (scapulohumeral, sternocostoclavicular, acromioclavicular) and 2 sliding spaces (subdeltoid bursa, scapulothoracic).

options: Is a saddle synovial joint
Has no articular disc
Unites the medial end of the clavicle with the manubrium and the first costal cartilage
Is a plane joint (arthrodia)
Allows wide rotational movements
questions.explanation: It is a saddle joint with a disc; the arthrodia of the shoulder complex is the acromioclavicular joint. Also false: "Has no articular disc"; "Allows wide rotational movements".

options: Is a saddle joint with a disc
Allows wide circumduction movements
Is held by the coracohumeral ligament
Is a plane joint (arthrodia)
Unites the lateral end of the clavicle with the acromion
questions.explanation: Saddle joint with a disc = sternocostoclavicular joint. Also false: "Is held by the coracohumeral ligament"; "Allows wide circumduction movements".

options: Is a false joint
Is a true synovial joint
Is a sliding space between the rib cage and the anterior surface of the scapula
Is formed between the acromion and the humeral head
Is a saddle joint
questions.explanation: It is a false joint: a gliding space between the thoracic wall and the scapula.

options: Is very stable
Is extremely fragile
Is the proximal joint of the thoracic limb
Is very mobile
Is a spheroid synovial joint (enarthrosis)
questions.explanation: The scapulohumeral joint is very mobile but fragile (unstable).

questions.stem: About the articular surfaces of the scapulohumeral joint:
options: The humeral head represents 1/3 of a sphere
The humeral head represents 2/3 of a sphere
The glenoid cavity has the glenoid notch on its anterior border
The glenoid cavity is spherical and deep
The glenoid cavity is oval and surrounded by the glenoid labrum
questions.explanation: The humeral head is 1/3 of a sphere (the femoral head is 2/3). The glenoid is oval and shallow, deepened by the labrum.

options: Its internal face is free and articular
Is a fibrocartilaginous ring on the rim of the glenoid cavity
Its peripheral face is covered with articular cartilage
Increases the depth of the glenoid cavity
Is round in section, with two faces
questions.explanation: The peripheral face extends the surface of the scapular neck; it is the external face that is articular and part of the glenoid surface. Also false: "Is round in section, with two faces"; "Its internal face is free and articular".

questions.stem: The capsule of the scapulohumeral joint:
options: Is a thin fibrous sleeve
Inserts on the coracoid process
Inserts on the anatomical and surgical necks of the humerus
Inserts on the peripheral face of the glenoid labrum
Is thick and very strong
questions.explanation: The capsule is thin, which is part of the joint's fragility.

options: Ends by two bundles on the greater and lesser tubercles
Ends by a single bundle on the surgical neck
Arises from the acromion
Is the strongest ligament of the scapulohumeral joint
Arises from the lateral border of the coracoid process
questions.explanation: Coracohumeral ligament: lateral border of the coracoid → greater tubercle (trochiter) and lesser tubercle (trochin).

options: The superior one ends below the surgical neck
The middle one ends on the lower part of the lesser tubercle
The inferior one ends on the upper part of the lesser tubercle
The foramen of Weitbrecht lies between the superior and middle ligaments
The foramen of Rouvière lies between the superior and middle ligaments
questions.explanation: Foramen of Rouvière is between the middle and inferior glenohumeral ligaments; both foramina are zones of capsular weakness. Also false: "The superior one ends below the surgical neck"; "The inferior one ends on the upper part of the lesser tubercle".

questions.stem: The weak zone of the shoulder capsule located between the middle and inferior glenohumeral ligaments is:
options: The foramen ovale of Weitbrecht
The foramen of Rouvière
The glenoid notch
The scapular notch
The bicipital groove
questions.explanation: Weitbrecht: between superior and middle; Rouvière: between middle and inferior.

questions.stem: Match the periarticular muscle (active ligament) of the scapulohumeral joint with its position:
options: Subscapularis: above
Subscapularis: in front
Supraspinatus: above
Infraspinatus, teres minor and teres major: behind
Supraspinatus: behind
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus above, infraspinatus/teres minor/teres major behind, subscapularis in front; plus long head of biceps, deltoid, triceps.

questions.stem: Which are periarticular serous bursae of the shoulder?
options: The subdeltoid bursa
The subcoracoid bursa
The subscapular bursa
The bicipital bursa
The infraspinatus bursa
questions.explanation: All five are listed: subscapular, bicipital, subdeltoid, subcoracoid and infraspinatus bursae; they facilitate gliding.

questions.stem: About movements of the scapulohumeral joint:
options: It has 3 degrees of freedom
Pure adduction is possible on its own
Flexion (antepulsion) occurs in the sagittal plane around a transverse axis
Abduction reaches 180° without the scapulothoracic joint
Extension (retropulsion) reaches 90°
questions.explanation: Pure adduction is not possible; combined with ante- or retropulsion it reaches 40°. Also false: "Abduction reaches 180° without the scapulothoracic joint"; "Extension (retropulsion) reaches 90°".

questions.stem: With participation of the scapulothoracic joint, shoulder abduction can reach:
questions.explanation: Abduction is 90° at the scapulohumeral joint alone and up to 180° with the scapulothoracic joint (same for flexion).

options: Rotations occur in the frontal plane
They occur in the transverse plane around a vertical axis
Medial rotation is limited to 80°, completed to 90° by an anterior tilt of the scapula
Lateral rotation is limited to 80°
Lateral rotation is limited to 30°
questions.explanation: Lateral rotation 30°, medial rotation 80° (90° with scapular tilt), in the transverse plane.
